gen-gf-sniglet-gf-m-plus-2: Distinctive is the word for Sniglet, whose terminals stop short of curling back in. But M PLUS 2, a sans with a gaping c and a fixed nib width, is the approachable half.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-m-plus-rounded-1c: Sniglet's terminals stop short of curling back in, and its quiet, level beat never leans on heavy accents. M PLUS Rounded 1c is an approachable sans-serif that stops its own strokes short in much the same way.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-mandali: Commanding up top, Sniglet keeps a level beat with no accents of weight in its letters. And Mandali, a plain sans with a generous entry into the e's eye, would keep paragraphs flowing without a snag.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-manjari: Distinctive and a bit bossy, Sniglet stops its terminals short of curling back in. Manjari, the sans-serif with wide, unclosed curves, holds the text while Sniglet grabs the attention.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-meera-inimai: Meera Inimai has the constant line of blueprint lettering, its open-ended curves leaving room to breathe under a commanding Sniglet heading. Meera Inimai, a plain sans, would make paragraphs feel unhurried and tidy.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-metrophobic: Metrophobic reads modern and clean, a sans-serif whose curves run smooth and unobstructed around each bend. And Sniglet earns its keep big and brief, where its stopped-short terminals can be seen.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-mina: Sniglet stops its terminals short of curling back in, giving the headings a quiet, level beat without heavy accents. Mina, a plain sans, keeps paragraphs light, drawn like stitched thread.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-mingzat: Mingzat is a contemporary sans-serif with curvy, unclamped letters, a loose counterpart to Sniglet and its sturdy diagonals. And across paragraphs it would flow loosely, never boxing the eye in.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-moderustic: Moderustic feels modern and contemporary, a sans whose curves are traced with a broad nib and left unfinished. Sniglet's single-width strokes up top make the broad-nibbed body feel looser.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-molengo: Contemporary in feel, Molengo is a sans-serif with wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp. And Sniglet, a monoweight display face, gives it a distinctive headline to sit beneath.
